docs.title: SciAgent
docs.text:
SciAgent is a platform where scientists query, harmonise and analyse multimodal biological data — microscopy imaging, genomics and clinical time series — through agentic workflows. Tools are governed, every decision is audited, and every release is gated by an evaluation suite.

Five-minute tour

make install && make test && make eval, then .venv/bin/sciagent query "How many nuclei are in IMG-0007?". See Getting started.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Reliable utility, not a demo. SLOs, runbooks and on-call ownership from day one.
  2. Governed by construction. The planner proposes; the policy engine disposes. No tool runs without an allow decision in the audit log.
  3. Reproducible. Datasets are versioned and content-hashed; tools are deterministic functions of their inputs; agent runs persist every step.
  4. Measured. Behaviour changes ship only when the evaluation gate passes.

docs.title: Risk register
docs.text:
Reviewed at every release planning meeting. Likelihood (L) and impact (I) are 1–5; score = L × I. Owner is the accountable role.

ID Risk L I Score Mitigation Owner Status R1 Agent states figures not supported by any analysis (hallucination) 3 5 15 Numeric-grounding output guardrail; numeric_grounding gate ≥ 95%; answers show tool steps Lead engineer Mitigated R2 Researcher accesses data outside their group via the agent 2 5 10 Policy engine on every call, default deny, governance eval tasks at 100%, audit log Lead engineer Mitigated R3 Prompt injection via questions or retrieved documents 3 4 12 Input guardrails; authorisation is structural (graph edge), not prompt-based; tools are read-only Lead engineer Mitigated R4 GPU scheduling contention delays inference 3 3 9 Dedicated tainted GPU node group; queue-depth autoscaling; rule-based fallback Platform Mitigated R5 GPU cost overrun 3 3 9 Scale-to-zero in dev; under-utilisation alert; cost-per-query dashboard Platform Monitoring R6 Data-access bottleneck from small files / cross-AZ reads on S3 3 3 9 Columnar Parquet with zstd; scheduled compaction; VPC gateway endpoint for S3 Data Mitigated R7 Model upgrade silently degrades answer quality 3 4 12 Eval-gated releases (ADR-0008); LLM-judge run against staging before prod Lead engineer Mitigated R8 PII leaks into logs or answers 2 5 10 Input PII blocking, output redaction, pseudonymised identifiers in all datasets Security Mitigated R9 Audit trail tampering 1 5 5 Hash chain with verification endpoint; RDS snapshots; least-privilege DB roles Security Mitigated R10 Single-person knowledge concentration 3 3 9 ADRs, runbooks, MkDocs, pairing on on-call Lead engineer Open R11 Upstream dependency breaking change (LangGraph, MCP SDK) 3 2 6 Pinned lower bounds, Dependabot, integration tests over in-process MCP Lead engineer Monitoring

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records
docs.text:
We record significant decisions using the format in ADR-0001. New ADRs are proposed in a PR and reviewed in the weekly design review; status moves from Proposed to Accepted (or Superseded by ADR-NNNN).

ADR Title Status 0001 Record architecture decisions Accepted 0002 Run the platform on Kubernetes (EKS) Accepted 0003 LangGraph for agent orchestration Accepted 0004 MCP servers for tool access Accepted 0005 Self-hosted LLM serving with vLLM Accepted 0006 Parquet/Delta lake on S3 Accepted 0007 PostgreSQL + pgvector for retrieval Accepted 0008 Evaluation-gated releases Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0001: Record architecture decisions
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-01-12

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The platform is built by a small team for several research groups over multiple years. Decisions made early (cluster, serving stack, data formats) constrain everything after, and the reasoning is easily lost.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We keep lightweight ADRs in docs/adr/, one file per decision, with Context, Decision, Consequences and Alternatives. Any change touching more than one component, adding an external dependency, or changing a security boundary requires an ADR in the same PR.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Design reviews have a written artefact to review. New contributors can read why things are the way they are. The cost is a short document per significant change.

docs.title: ADR-0002: Run the platform on Kubernetes (EKS)
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-01-14

docs.title: Context
docs.text: We need to run stateless services (API, MCP servers), GPU inference, and batch pipelines with independent scaling, isolation between research groups' workloads, and reproducible environments for dev, staging and prod.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Amazon EKS with three managed node groups — system, cpu-workers and a tainted gpu-inference group — provisioned by Terraform. Workloads are packaged as one Helm chart. IAM access to S3 and Secrets Manager uses IRSA with one role per workload.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• GPU capacity can scale to zero in dev and scale on queue depth in prod.
  • One deployment model for services, inference and Airflow workers.
  • We take on Kubernetes operational complexity; mitigated with managed node groups, managed add-ons and a single chart.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• ECS/Fargate: simpler, but weaker GPU scheduling and no first-class operator ecosystem.
  • SageMaker endpoints for inference: easy to start, but higher per-hour GPU cost and a second deployment model.

docs.title: ADR-0003: LangGraph for agent orchestration
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-01-20

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Agent behaviour must be inspectable and governable: every tool call has to pass an authorisation step that the model cannot skip, runs need step limits, and we need to test individual transitions.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Model the agent as an explicit LangGraph StateGraph with nodes for input guardrails, retrieval, planning, authorisation, execution and output guardrails. Authorisation is a graph edge, not a prompt instruction.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Governance is structural: there is no path from plan to act that bypasses authorize.
  • Each node is a plain method, unit-testable with scripted LLM responses.
  • We depend on LangGraph's state/reducer semantics; the graph is small enough to port.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• Free-form ReAct loop: less code, but governance would rely on prompt compliance.
  • Hand-written state machine: viable; LangGraph gives us checkpointing and streaming without maintaining them ourselves.

docs.title: ADR-0004: MCP servers for tool access
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-01-27

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Models and pipelines are owned by different groups and change at different speeds. The agent needs a stable, typed contract to discover and call them, and the same tools should be usable from other MCP-capable clients (notebooks, IDE assistants).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Expose tools through three domain MCP servers (imaging, genomics, clinical) over Streamable HTTP. Tool schemas are generated from the shared pydantic registry so the agent plans against exactly the schema the server validates. Policy is enforced in the agent gateway, before the call leaves the agent.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Domains deploy and scale independently; a failing imaging server does not affect clinical.
  • One definition per tool; schema drift between client and server is impossible.
  • MCP servers are not themselves an authorisation boundary — they are reachable only from the API via NetworkPolicy.

docs.title: ADR-0005: Self-hosted LLM serving with vLLM
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-02-03

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Prompts include identifiers and summaries of clinical and genomic data that must not leave our AWS account. We need predictable latency (p95 < 300 ms for planning calls) and cost control as usage grows.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Serve open-weight instruction models with vLLM on the gpu-inference node group, exposed through its OpenAI-compatible API. The agent talks to it through OpenAICompatibleLLM, so the model is a configuration value. A deterministic rule-based planner is the offline fallback and CI reference.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Data stays in-account; no third-party processor agreements needed for inference.
  • Continuous batching and prefix caching give high throughput per GPU; autoscaling on vllm:num_requests_waiting matches capacity to demand.
  • We own model upgrades; every model change goes through the evaluation gate (ADR-0008).

docs.title: ADR-0006: Parquet/Delta lake on S3
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-02-10

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Data volumes are in the terabytes, mostly append-heavy, read by batch analytics and by tools that need column subsets. We need versioning and reproducibility.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Store curated data as Parquet (zstd) on S3 with <zone>/<modality>/<dataset>/v=<n>/ layout, with Delta Lake for tables needing ACID upserts. Every publish registers a new catalog version with a layout-independent content checksum and lineage.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Cheap storage with lifecycle tiering; columnar reads for tools.
  • Analyses can pin a dataset version and verify its checksum.
  • Small-file compaction is an operational task handled by a scheduled pipeline.

docs.title: ADR-0007: PostgreSQL + pgvector for retrieval
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-02-17

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The agent retrieves dataset descriptions and tool documentation (tens of thousands of documents, not billions). We already run PostgreSQL for the catalog, runs and audit log.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Store embeddings in a pgvector table with an HNSW index (cosine distance) in the same RDS instance. Locally and in tests, an in-memory store implements the same interface.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No additional stateful service to operate; transactional consistency with the catalog.
  • Retrieval scales comfortably for our corpus; revisit if it grows by orders of magnitude.

docs.title: ADR-0008: Evaluation-gated releases
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-02-24

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Prompt, model and tool changes can silently degrade answers. Unit tests do not catch "the agent picked the wrong analysis" or "the agent stated a number it did not compute".

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Maintain a curated task suite (categories: imaging, genomics, clinical, harmonisation, governance, safety). Each task is checked automatically (status, tool selection, policy enforcement, numeric grounding against reference tool calls) and graded by an LLM judge against a rubric. Low-confidence results go to a human review queue. Releases are blocked unless thresholds in evals/gate.yaml are met; safety and governance require 100%.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Regressions are caught before deploy, and every release has an evaluation report.
  • Curating tasks is ongoing work, owned by the groups who use the platform.
  • The judge itself can drift; its agreement with human reviewers is tracked per release.

docs.title: Agent layer
docs.text:
The agent is a LangGraph StateGraph defined in sciagent/agent/graph.py.

stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> guard_input
  guard_input --> [*]: blocked
  guard_input --> retrieve
  retrieve --> plan
  plan --> authorize: tool calls
  plan --> guard_output: final answer
  plan --> max_steps: step budget exhausted
  authorize --> act
  act --> plan
  guard_output --> [*]
  max_steps --> [*]

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text: Node Responsibility guard_input Prompt-injection, PII and length checks; blocked runs end immediately and are audited retrieve Top-k catalog/tool documents from the vector store into the system prompt plan One LLM call with OpenAI-style tool schemas; records token usage authorize Policy decision per call (role, group, classification, budget, row limits) + audit act Executes allowed calls through the ToolGateway; errors become tool messages guard_output PII redaction and numeric grounding against tool outputs

docs.title: LLM backends
docs.text:
• vLLM (SCIAGENT_LLM_BACKEND=vllm): OpenAI-compatible chat completions with tool_choice=auto. The served model is configured in the Helm values.
  • Rule-based planner (default locally and in CI): deterministic intent routing and templated summaries. It is the reference agent for the regression suite, which keeps CI fast and free of GPU dependencies while the LLM-judge run uses staging.

docs.title: Tool gateways
docs.text: LocalToolGateway calls the registry in-process. McpToolGateway routes each tool to its domain's MCP server over Streamable HTTP. Both share the same registry for schemas, so a tool is defined once and validated identically regardless of transport.

docs.title: Zones
docs.text: Zone Contents Writers Readers raw Landed source extracts, immutable ingestion Airflow curated Validated, harmonised Parquet/Delta tables, versioned v=<n> Airflow API, MCP servers artifacts Evaluation reports, model outputs API, CI everyone (read)

docs.title: Pipelines
docs.text:
src/sciagent/data/pipelines.yaml declares 40 pipelines across imaging (segmentation, features), genomics (variants, scRNA QC), clinical vitals (5 signals × 3 sites), lab harmonisation and outcome registry snapshots. Each has a schedule and quality checks.

extract → validate (min_rows, not_null, range, unique) → publish (lake) → register (catalog)

The runner is engine-agnostic: the Airflow DAG factory in dags/ wraps the same run_pipeline call used by the CLI and the tests.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
• Every publish creates a new dataset version with a content checksum that is independent of file layout, plus lineage (pipeline, kind, parameters).
  • Re-running a pipeline on unchanged inputs yields the same checksum; tests assert this.

docs.title: Harmonisation
docs.text: sciagent/data/harmonise.py maps site-local lab codes to LOINC and converts to canonical UCUM units (e.g. °F → Cel, mg/dL → mmol/L for glucose). Unmapped or unconvertible records are kept with an explicit status rather than silently dropped.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text:
Env Cluster Node groups Notes dev sciagent-dev system, cpu-workers, gpu-inference (min 0) single NAT, scale-to-zero GPUs staging sciagent-staging as prod, smaller receives every release first prod sciagent-prod system, cpu-workers, gpu-inference Multi-AZ RDS, manual approval

Infrastructure is Terraform (infra/terraform/envs/<env>), applied from CI with OIDC role assumption. Workloads are deployed with the Helm chart in deploy/helm/sciagent.

docs.title: Release flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  tag[git tag vX.Y.Z] --> gate[eval gate]
  gate --> build[build + push images<br/>SBOM, provenance]
  build --> staging[helm upgrade staging<br/>smoke test]
  staging --> approval{manual approval}
  approval --> prod[helm upgrade prod --atomic]

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
• Metrics: /metrics on every service, scraped via ServiceMonitors; vLLM and DCGM exporters for GPU metrics.
  • SLO alerts: multi-window burn-rate alerts for 99.9% API availability and p95 latency (deploy/monitoring/prometheus/rules).
  • Dashboards: deploy/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/sciagent-overview.json.
  • Logs: structured JSON with request_id correlation.

docs.title: GPU cost controls
docs.text:
• GPU nodes are tainted; only vLLM tolerates them.
  • vLLM autoscales on queue depth rather than CPU, and dev scales to zero.
  • The GPUUnderutilised alert flags nodes below 20% utilisation for an hour.

docs.title: Task format
docs.text:
{"id": "surv-02", "category": "clinical",
 "question": "Kaplan-Meier survival for sepsis patients by treatment arm, with a log-rank test.",
 "expected": {"tools": ["survival_analysis"], "answer_contains": ["log-rank"],
              "numbers": [{"tool": "survival_analysis", "arguments": {"diagnosis": "sepsis"},
                           "field": "logrank.p_value"}]},
 "rubric": "Reports median survival per group and log-rank p-value"}

numbers are recomputed from reference tool calls at evaluation time, so expected values never drift from the data.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
Check Meaning status completed / blocked as expected tool_selection expected tools ⊆ tools called policy_enforced expected denials happened answer_contains / answer_excludes required / forbidden phrases numeric_grounding reference figures appear in the answer judge 1–5 rubric score (heuristic in CI, served model with --judge llm)

Failures, and passes scored below 3 by the judge, are exported to review_queue.csv with empty reviewer_score/reviewer_notes columns for human review.

docs.title: Release gate
docs.text: evals/gate.yaml sets thresholds (overall pass rate, per-category floors — safety and governance must be 100% — check rates, judge mean, p95 latency). The eval-gate workflow runs on every PR touching src/ or evals/ and is a required job of release.yml.

docs.title: Tool policy
docs.text:
sciagent/governance/policies.yaml is the single source of truth for which principals may call which tools. Unknown tools are denied by default.

Attribute Effect group Caller must belong to the data group (imaging, genomics, clinical) roles Allowed roles (researcher, analyst, admin) classification restricted tools require an admin max_calls_per_run Per-run budget to bound cost and runaway loops max_rows Upper bound on limit arguments

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text: Every authorisation decision, direct tool call, dataset registration and guardrail event is appended to audit_events. Each row stores prev_hash and hash = sha256(prev_hash || canonical_json(event)); GET /v1/audit/verify and sciagent audit-verify replay the chain and return the first tampered sequence number.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
Stage Check Action Input prompt injection patterns block Input PII (email, phone, IBAN, DOB) block Input > 4 000 characters block Output PII redact Output numbers not traceable to tool outputs or the question flag in answer

All guardrail events increment sciagent_guardrail_blocks_total{rule,stage}.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  user[Researcher] -->|x-api-key| api[FastAPI gateway]
  api --> agent[LangGraph agent]
  agent -->|authorize| policy[Policy engine]
  policy --> audit[(Audit log<br/>hash chain)]
  agent -->|plan| llm[vLLM]
  agent -->|Streamable HTTP| mcp[MCP servers<br/>imaging · genomics · clinical]
  mcp --> lake[(S3 lake<br/>curated zone)]
  airflow[Airflow · 40 DAGs] --> lake
  airflow --> catalog[(PostgreSQL catalog<br/>+ pgvector)]
  api --> catalog

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Runtime Scales on Notes api Deployment, 3+ replicas CPU / RPS Stateless; sessions are runs in PostgreSQL mcp-{imaging,genomics,clinical} Deployment per domain CPU Independent release and blast radius per domain vllm GPU Deployment on g5 nodes queue depth (vllm:num_requests_waiting) Scale-to-zero in dev Airflow KubernetesExecutor tasks DAGs generated from pipelines.yaml PostgreSQL 16 RDS Multi-AZ — catalog, runs, audit, embeddings (pgvector HNSW) S3 raw / curated / artifacts buckets — SSE-KMS, versioning, lifecycle tiers

docs.title: Request lifecycle
docs.text:
1. The API authenticates the key, creates an agent_runs row and invokes the agent.
  2. The agent runs input guardrails, retrieves catalog context, and asks the LLM to plan.
  3. Each proposed tool call is evaluated by the policy engine and written to the audit log.
  4. Allowed calls go through the gateway (MCP in cluster); results are appended to the conversation and the agent plans again, up to agent_max_steps.
  5. Output guardrails redact PII and flag ungrounded numbers; the run is persisted with all steps, token counts and latency.

docs.title: Package map
docs.text:
sciagent/
  api/          FastAPI app, routers, middleware, dependency container
  agent/        LangGraph graph, tool gateways, prompts
  tools/        tool registry and the 8 scientific tools
  mcp_servers/  MCP server factory + entry points
  governance/   policy engine, guardrails, audit log, policies.yaml
  catalog/      SQLAlchemy models and repositories
  data/         synthetic sources, harmonisation, lake I/O, pipelines
  retrieval/    embeddings and vector stores
  llm/          vLLM client, rule-based planner
  eval/         task schema, runner, judges, release gate

docs.title: Adding a pipeline
docs.text:
1. If the source is new, add an extractor to EXTRACTORS in src/sciagent/data/pipelines.py returning a list of row dicts.
  2. Declare the pipeline in src/sciagent/data/pipelines.yaml with an id, kind, modality, group, cron schedule, params and quality checks.
  3. Run it locally: sciagent pipelines run <id>.
  4. The Airflow DAG sciagent__<id> is generated automatically on the next scheduler parse.

The test suite asserts that every declared pipeline passes its own quality checks.

docs.title: Adding a tool
docs.text:
1. Implement a pydantic input model and a pure function in the relevant module under src/sciagent/tools/ (or a new module), returning a JSON-serialisable dict. Constrain identifiers with pattern= and numeric arguments with ge/le; these constraints are carried into the MCP schema.
  2. Register it by appending a Tool(...) to that module's TOOLS list, choosing the MCP server (imaging, genomics, clinical).
  3. Govern it: add an entry to src/sciagent/governance/policies.yaml with its data group, budget and row limits. Tools missing from the policy are denied.
  4. Test it: unit tests for the scientific logic, plus a policy test.
  5. Evaluate it: add tasks to evals/tasks/<category>.jsonl, including at least one numbers check and one governance task where the call must be denied.
  6. Open a PR; the eval gate must pass.

docs.title: API usage
docs.text:
All endpoints except /healthz, /readyz and /metrics require an x-api-key header. OpenAPI docs are served at /docs.

Method Path Purpose POST /v1/query Run the agent on a question; returns the persisted run with steps GET /v1/runs, /v1/runs/{id} Run history (own runs; admins see all) GET /v1/tools Tool specs with an allowed flag for the caller POST /v1/tools/{name}:call Direct, policy-checked tool invocation GET /v1/datasets, /v1/datasets/{id} Catalog, filtered to the caller's groups POST /v1/datasets Register a dataset version (admin) GET /v1/search?q= Semantic search over tools and datasets GET /v1/audit/events, /v1/audit/verify Audit trail and chain verification (admin)

Errors share one shape:

{"error": {"code": "policy_denied", "message": "user not in data group 'genomics'",
           "details": {"tool": "annotate_variants"}}, "request_id": "4b1f..."}

import httpx

client = httpx.Client(base_url="http://localhost:8000", headers={"x-api-key": "dev-researcher-key"})
run = client.post("/v1/query", json={"question": "Run single-cell QC on SC-0003"}).json()
print(run["answer"])
for step in run["steps"]:
    print(step["tool"], step["decision"], step.get("latency_ms"))

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or 3.12 and uv (pip works too)
  • Docker (optional) for the full local stack

docs.title: Install and verify
docs.text:
make install   # .venv with sciagent[dev,docs]
make lint typecheck test
make eval      # curated evaluation suite against evals/gate.yaml

docs.title: Ask questions locally
docs.text:
.venv/bin/sciagent query "Summarise the high impact variants for WGS-0002"
.venv/bin/sciagent query "Does survival differ by sex in pneumonia patients?" --json

Use --api-key dev-admin-key to act as an administrator. Keys and their groups are configured with SCIAGENT_API_KEYS (see .env.example).

docs.title: Populate the catalog
docs.text:
.venv/bin/sciagent pipelines list
.venv/bin/sciagent pipelines run all     # 40 pipelines → .lake/curated/... + catalog rows

docs.title: Run services
docs.text:
make run    # API on :8000 with in-process tools
make mcp    # the three MCP servers on :8101-8103
SCIAGENT_TOOL_TRANSPORT=mcp make run   # API calling tools over MCP

Or everything at once: docker compose up --build.

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
Each alert in deploy/monitoring/prometheus/rules links here. Every runbook follows the same shape: Impact → Diagnose → Mitigate → Follow up.

  • API availability burn rate
  • API latency
  • LLM serving latency / queue
  • Tool error ratio
  • Guardrail block spike
  • Pipeline failures
  • GPU under-utilised
  • Audit chain broken

docs.title: API availability burn rate
docs.text:
Impact: researchers receive 5xx responses; the 99.9% error budget is being consumed.

Diagnose 1. Grafana → SciAgent overview → error ratio by route. Is it one route or all? 2. kubectl -n sciagent get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/component=api — restarts, OOMKills? 3. /readyz reports the failing dependency (database, tools). 4. 502s on /v1/query usually mean a tool server or vLLM is failing — check those panels.

Mitigate: roll back with helm rollback sciagent -n sciagent; scale the API; fail over RDS if the database check is red.

Follow up: postmortem if more than 25% of the monthly budget was burned.

docs.title: API latency
docs.text:
Diagnose: split p95 by route. /v1/query latency is dominated by LLM and tool calls — compare sciagent_tool_call_duration_seconds and vLLM latency. Other routes point at the database (check RDS Performance Insights).

Mitigate: scale API/MCP replicas; reduce SCIAGENT_AGENT_MAX_STEPS temporarily.

docs.title: LLM serving latency / queue
docs.text:
Diagnose: vllm:num_requests_waiting rising with flat replica count means the HPA is capped or GPU nodes cannot be scheduled (kubectl get nodes -l workload=gpu-inference, cluster-autoscaler logs, EC2 capacity for g5).

Mitigate: raise vllm.autoscaling.maxReplicas; as a last resort set SCIAGENT_LLM_BACKEND=rule on the API to fall back to the deterministic planner.

docs.title: Tool error ratio
docs.text:
Diagnose: sciagent_tool_calls_total{outcome="error"} by tool. invalid outcomes mean the planner is producing bad arguments (check recent model/prompt changes and the latest evaluation report); error outcomes mean the tool itself failed (MCP server logs).

Mitigate: roll back the offending MCP server or model; remove the tool from policies.yaml to disable it platform-wide.

docs.title: Guardrail block spike
docs.text:
Diagnose: sciagent_guardrail_blocks_total by rule. Query recent guardrail.input audit events (GET /v1/audit/events) to see whether this is abuse, a client bug, or a false positive (e.g. a new identifier format matching a PII pattern).

Mitigate: for false positives, add a guardrail unit test reproducing it, fix the pattern, and ship through the eval gate.

docs.title: Pipeline failures
docs.text:
Diagnose: Airflow UI → failing DAG sciagent__<pipeline>. quality_gate failures list the violated checks; publish failures are usually S3/IRSA permissions or schema changes.

Mitigate: the previous dataset version remains current in the catalog, so consumers are unaffected. Fix the source or the check, then clear the task.

docs.title: GPU under-utilised
docs.text:
Impact: cost, not availability.

Diagnose: DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL per node vs. request rate. Common causes: HPA minReplicas too high after a load test; a stuck pod holding a GPU.

Mitigate: lower minReplicas (dev: 0); delete stuck pods.

docs.title: Audit chain broken
docs.text:
Impact: possible tampering with the audit trail — treat as a security incident.

  1. Run sciagent audit-verify to get the first bad sequence number.
  2. Restrict write access to the database; snapshot RDS immediately.
  3. Compare the affected rows against the latest RDS snapshot and CloudTrail/RDS logs.
  4. Notify the security officer; do not "repair" the chain in place.
